Decipher
  • SuperMemo SM-2 Spaced Repetition Engine
  • View page source

SuperMemo SM-2 Spaced Repetition Engine

DECIPHER incorporates the SuperMemo SM-2 spaced repetition algorithm to optimize vocabulary retention and counteract Ebbinghaus’s forgetting curve.

Mathematical Formulation

The algorithm calculates the review interval ($I$) and ease factor ($EF$) based on the user’s recall quality rating ($q in {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}$).

1. Interval Progression

For a given repetition count $n$:

\[\begin{split}I(n) = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{for } n = 1 \\ 6 & \text{for } n = 2 \\ \text{round}(I(n-1) \times EF) & \text{for } n > 2 \end{cases}\end{split}\]

If the recall grade $q < 3$ (lapse): * The repetition count $n$ resets to $0$. * The next interval $I$ resets to $1$ day.

2. Ease Factor Update

The ease factor reflects item difficulty and updates after every review:

\[EF' = EF + (0.1 - (5 - q) \times (0.08 + (5 - q) \times 0.02))\]

  • Minimum Ease Factor Bound: $EF’ ge 1.3$.

  • Initial card ease factor defaults to $2.5$.

Recall Grade Scale ($q$)

Grade ($q$)

Quality

Description

5

Perfect

Instant, flawless recall with zero hesitation.

4

Good

Correct response after brief hesitation.

3

Pass

Correct response recalled with serious difficulty.

2

Hard Fail

Incorrect response; correct answer felt familiar upon reveal.

1

Fail

Incorrect response; correct answer remembered only upon reveal.

0

Blackout

Complete failure of recall; total unfamiliarity.

Review Queue Manager Architecture

The SRSQueueManager class in modules/srs.js orchestrates card lifecycles:

  • Card State Schema: * repetitions: Integer count of consecutive successful reviews. * interval: Scheduled interval in days. * ef: Floating-point ease factor ($ge 1.3$). * lastReviewed: Epoch millisecond timestamp of last review. * dueDate: Epoch millisecond timestamp when card is due (lastReviewed + interval * 86,400,000).

  • Card Tier Classification: * New / Learning: $I < 6$ days. * Reviewing: $6 le I < 21$ days. * Mature: $I ge 21$ days.

Weak Words Drill Room Integration

Words with high failure rates are automatically routed to the Weak Words queue (modules/drill.js). The drill engine categorizes mistakes into: 1. spelling_typo: Levenshtein distance $le 2$. 2. near_miss: Partial phonetic or morphological match. 3. confused_definition: Mismatched vocabulary definition. 4. unanswered: Timeout or blank submission.

Graduation from the Weak Words queue requires 3 consecutive successful recalls.
